stories.title: Venomous Primate Believed Extinct for 100 Years Was Hiding in Plain Sight All Along
stories.label: animals
stories.summary: Meet the Bangka slow loris, a tiny big-eyed primate that scientists feared had vanished from the Indonesian island of Bangka a century ago. It turns out these shy creatures were quietly surviving all along, thanks in large part to a local wildlife group that has been rescuing and releasing them back into the forest. Confirmed sightings now show a real, living population, not just a memory in old field notes. It's a wonderful reminder that some 'lost' species are just waiting to be noticed and protected. This one even has a surprising trick: its bite carries venom, making it one of the only venomous primates on Earth.
stories.why_good: A species long feared extinct has been confirmed alive and recovering, thanks to real on-the-ground conservation work that already happened.

stories.title: Adventurer Finally Hugs Mom After 28-Year Walk Around the World From Home in UK
stories.label: people
stories.summary: A British man named Karl Bushby set off in 1998 on an incredible goal: to walk all the way around the world and return home using only his own two feet. After 28 years and roughly 31,000 miles crossing countries and continents, he finally made it back to his hometown of Hull. Waiting for him was his mother, and the two shared a long, tearful hug as neighbors and media gathered to welcome him home. It's a beautiful reminder of what patience, determination, and love of family can accomplish over a lifetime.
stories.why_good: A real person actually completed an extraordinary personal journey and was reunited with his family, pure human triumph with no suffering, crime, or politics involved.
